thread:
Maria K: Heads up — ran a cross-GPU attention sweep (A100 / H100 / L40S) focused on Flash variants vs paged/fused attention. Seq len sweep 128/512/2048, batch sizes 1/8/32. TL;DR: L40S favors fused at mid-lens, H100 shows a microburst on paged at bsz32+; KV cache thrash surfaced for long-seq chat workloads.

Kevin L: Nice. Any perf graphs?

Maria K: Pasted a quick excerpt from the run:
```
cmd: ./bench_attn --model=llama2-7b --kernels=flash,paged,fused --gpus=A100,H100,L40S --seq=128,512,2048 --bs=1,8,32 --iters=200
A100 seq2048 bsz1 flash: 82 ms / step
A100 seq2048 bsz8 fused: 95 ms / step
H100 seq2048 bsz32 paged: 310 ms / step (latency tail ~600ms)
L40S seq512 bsz8 fused: 40 ms / step (best)
logs: /tmp/attn-sweep-3487654322.log
```

Sanjay R: That H100 paged tail is alarming. Did you capture kernel selection flips?

Maria K: Yes — selector flipped between paged and flash around 160 tokens for bsz32 on H100. The decision heuristic picked paged due to predicted memory pressure but we saw KV cache thrash: excessive evictions when parallel requests had mixed seq lengths.

Eva T: Can you share the sample trace? I want to see where prefetch missed.

Maria K: Pasted a small stack trace snippet from the tracer:
```
[2026-03-16 15:02:01] select_kernel: chosen=paged variant=paged_fused_prefetch
[2026-03-16 15:02:01] kvcache: evict batch=3 keys=120 miss=0.28
[2026-03-16 15:02:01] runtime: fallback to memcpy-path due to allocation spike
```

Kevin L: Sounds like batching heuristic isn't weighting seq-length variance enough. If one concurrent request is long, it biases for paged, but short seqs pay the cost.

Sanjay R: Agreed. Proposed quick fixes: 1) add per-batch seq-variance penalty in selector score, 2) detect KV eviction rate > 0.2 and prefer flash/fused, 3) telemetry flag to log selection confidence.

Maria K: Implemented 1 locally — reran with seq-mix synthetic workload (50% 128, 50% 2048) on H100 bsz32: paged selection dropped 70% -> latency median improved from 330ms to 190ms. Still seeing tail spikes at 99th (480ms).

perf-bot: :rotating_light: anomaly detected — KV eviction rate spike (0.31) on H100 node h100-prod-12 during run 3487654322, correlates with paged selection periods.

Eva T: Can we try aggressive prefix caching for mixed workloads? Maybe reduce eviction by keeping hot prefixes pinned.

Maria K: I added a temporary pin for first 64 tokens — rerun on A100/H100/L40S: 99th improved ~12% across the board, median same. L40S fused still wins for seq512 workloads.

Kevin L: Good. For next steps: please open a perf-regression PR with the selector-penalty heuristic + telemetry flag. Also add a microbenchmark to the nightly suite that mixes seq lengths (1/8/32) to catch this.

Sanjay R: I'll draft the PR and include the delta numbers and a kernel-choice heatmap.

Maria K: Uploaded artifacts to /artifacts/attn_sweep/3487654322/ (heatmaps, logs, kv-traces). Ping me if you need the raw GPU traces.

Eva T: :thumbsup: Thanks — this explains recent canary blips.

Kevin L: Adding note for release: include a config knob for "selector_seq_variance_penalty" default 0.2. We can tune postrollout.

Maria K: Sounds good. I'll open an RFC and attach the benchmark data.

perf-bot: Latest run summary: median latency improved 14% after selector tweak; regression risk flagged low.

Sanjay R: Filing follow-ups: 1) autotune penalty value, 2) nightly mixed-seq test, 3) prefetched-prefix experiment cleanup.

Maria K: Thanks team — I'll share the PR link when ready.
